For the owner — internal review scaffold, never shipped

Qurova, or the open-licence fallback — read the real headlines before you choose

This page is an internal review scaffold. It never ships. The candidate faces below load live from Google Fonts' CDN for this review only — the moment a face is chosen it gets vendored into design-system/assets/fonts/ before it goes anywhere near production, for exactly the reason recorded as conflict C25 in docs/build/LEGAL-PLACEHOLDER-CHECKLIST.md: hotlinking a third-party font CDN in production leaks a visitor's IP address and user-agent before consent.

The recommendation, argued in full in .planning/ADR-009-qurova-webfont-licence.md, is to buy the $69 Prioritype Web Font licence and keep Qurova. This page exists as insurance in case that purchase does not happen — every string below is taken verbatim from the live mocks, set at the sizes, weights and tracking Qurova is actually used at, so the choice is between rendered options rather than an abstract typographic question asked under launch pressure.

It exists to make one open decision concrete. Nothing on it is production markup, and it carries none of the four-language requirement Law 03 sets for shipped surfaces — it is English only, on purpose, as the internal-review exception that law names. Outfit and Manrope load from Google Fonts' CDN so you can see them rendered without vendoring three families to compare them. That is acceptable for one reviewer's own browser loading this internal page — it would not be acceptable in production, which is exactly the C25 finding above. No candidate on this page — and not Qurova either — contains a single Arabic glyph. An Arabic row would render in a browser or system fallback and prove nothing about any of these faces. The Arabic display face is a separate open item, recorded in ADR-009, and this page does not attempt to answer it.
Qurova Current brand

Commercial retail face, Prioritype Co. All rights reserved; the font files carry no licence description and no licence URL at all. Not open-licensed. Full provenance and the vendor's published Web Font tier ($69) are in ADR-009.
Poppins Already vendored

SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1 — verified with no network call at all, directly from the font files' own name table, and from design-system/assets/fonts/OFL.txt vendored in this same pass. What you give up: the display voice and the UI voice collapse into one typeface — a real loss, not a neutral simplification.
Outfit Google Fonts

Open Font License (SIL OFL 1.1). Verified at fonts.google.com/specimen/Outfit/license on 2026-08-19; that specimen page renders client-side, so the licence text was cross-checked against the same family's own OFL.txt in Google's github.com/google/fonts source repository (path ofl/outfit/OFL.txt), same date. What you give up: a geometric grotesque with no history in this brand's mocks — every existing display setting has to be re-judged by eye rather than carried forward.
Manrope Google Fonts

Open Font License (SIL OFL 1.1). Verified at fonts.google.com/specimen/Manrope/license on 2026-08-19; also cross-checked, same date, against github.com/google/fonts path ofl/manrope/OFL.txt. What you give up: Manrope's tighter, rounder terminals read softer than Qurova's cut — the confident, plain brand voice would lean gentler than the mocks were built to.

Tagline — “Ride with class” Set artwork, never re-set in type by any page — shown here once for context, not as a live comparison across candidates.

Ride with class

Buy the $69 Prioritype Web Font licence and keep Qurova. Against a 2–3 week launch and a bound design system whose display face is the brand voice, $69 is not a real trade-off. The two questions that have to go to Prioritype in writing before the purchase — what covers web usage above the 100,000 monthly pageview cap, and whether the licence is perpetual or annual — are recorded in ADR-009 and do not block buying the licence itself.
What you are giving up, per candidate
  • Poppins — the display voice and the UI voice become one typeface; nothing on the page reads as distinctly "brand" versus "interface" anymore.
  • Outfit — a competent geometric grotesque with no history in this brand; every existing display setting across 30+ screens has to be re-judged by eye rather than carried forward as-is.
  • Manrope — softer, rounder terminals than Qurova's cut; the confident, plain voice the copy is written to land in would read gentler than the mocks were built for.

Full reasoning, the vendor's price list and both open questions for the foundry: see .planning/ADR-009-qurova-webfont-licence.md.
